QF.id: Concept and Role of Mutual Fund_23

question.text: Mr. Verma has Rs. 20 lakh to invest for 3 months while he waits for a property deal to close. He wants minimal risk and instant access to funds. His distributor recommends a Long Duration Debt Fund citing "higher yields." Which of the following best describes the issue with this recommendation?

answer.text: A Long Duration Fund carries significant interest rate risk and is unsuitable for a 3-month horizon; a Liquid Fund or Overnight Fund would be more appropriate
Long Duration Funds are perfectly suitable because they invest in government securities which are risk-free
The recommendation is fine because all debt funds carry the same level of risk regardless of duration
Mr. Verma should invest in an equity fund instead since 3 months is sufficient for equity markets to generate positive returns

explanation.text: The Logic: Per pages 50-51 and 258, a Long Duration Fund has a Macaulay duration greater than 7 years and its NAV is highly sensitive to interest-rate changes. Per page 290, liquid funds suit very short parking horizons (up to 91 days) with high liquidity and negligible volatility. For a 3-month horizon needing capital safety and liquidity, a Liquid Fund or Overnight Fund matches the horizon to the fund's duration profile (page 296). The Trap: Option B ignores that even government securities carry duration/interest-rate risk. Option C overlooks the fact that debt fund risk varies sharply with duration. Option D is unsuitable for a 3-month capital-safety horizon and a short equity exposure can easily produce capital loss. Note: Always match the fund's Macaulay duration to the client's investment horizon rather than choosing a debt category on yield alone.
